BIND-REQUEST-PAYLOAD-CAP-01.goal: The bind loop, the night driver's bounded wait for sustained quiet before permitting an unattended measurement, sends requests to worker processes (child processes that perform individual checks) on the command line: `scripts/run_night.py` `_bind_argv` puts the whole static receipt (the recorded results of checks performed once before binding) into the `--request` argument as JSON. This is the one uncapped payload crossing a process boundary in a design whose result frame (a length-delimited reply sent through a pipe) is capped at 256 KiB. A request over the operating-system kernel's argument-length limit fails closed to `night_probe_error` (the refusal code for a failed probe), which is outside D-182's eligible successor set (the refusal outcomes that permit a fresh replacement night after zero capture), so such a night gets no successor.

THE ROW'S STATED ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS IS CONTRADICTED BY THE REPRODUCTION AND SHOULD NOT BE ASSUMED BY THE CURING SEAT. The goal field says temp-path bytes leak into the artifacts. CI-SHARD-RUNNER-FILE-BASED-01.goal: Replace the hosted continuous-integration shard runner, the program that selects and runs one subset of automated tests, with a file-based or importable runner. It currently feeds its test script to Python on standard input. COURIER-LOCK-OWNERSHIP-FLOCK-01.goal: Replace the night courier's lock, the file that marks which process may send the night's report email, with an operating-system advisory lock (`flock`) held on one persistent file that is never deleted. The current lock is created empty and then filled with the owner's process id and time; in the interval between those two steps a second caller reads an empty file, judges the lock stale, deletes it, creates its own, and both callers send. The dead-man process (the backstop that reports when the courier never did) must use the same lock probe, so a corrupt, empty or old lock file is no longer permission to take over; a hung owner becomes an explicit recovery case. The dead-man's own reporting block also gets the shared best-effort guard the courier gained in fix round 4 of the evidence executor, and the two remaining prerequisites named by consult 79 Q5 (chain-exit persistence before the boundary; process creation itself) are stated as the accepted limits. Contract-bearing: it changes the stale-lock takeover semantics the handback and runbook describe, so a cold-gate packet precedes implementation.

acceptance.summary: Design adopted from the 2026-09-16 pre-decision consult (record 02): cure B plus a hard custody deadline; cure A deferred to a separately specified authenticated-local-store change, and its recorded-hashes-only variant rejected. (1) Every night-path custody verification (reservation readiness, capture-writer preflight, under-lease custody reads) runs in a read-only worker with no writer authority under ONE shared monotonic deadline (proposed 120 s whole-pass, clipped to end at least 10 s before the exclusive window end; the launchd dry run must show the real corpus fits); full artifact hashing is kept on success. Expiry raises the typed refusal calibration_ledger_custody_timeout (RefusalCode.LEDGER_CUSTODY_TIMEOUT, operational, arm-blocking, stop-preserved, exit 2, terminal result night_stopped_preserved) BEFORE any append: for a fresh reservation the ledger and head-pin bytes are unchanged and no intent or session row is added; a pre-existing session and its recovery evidence are preserved; the lease is released on unwinding and another process can reacquire it. (2) The refusal reaches the courier: the writer publishes the structured payload to a night-owned calibration-refusal.json, the driver registers night_calibration_refused, writes a REFUSED result carrying the exact code, and the courier reports the code, budget and elapsed time. (3) Arm admission requires a successful verify-only run of the shared reservation preflight FROM A TEMPORARY LAUNCHAGENT in the production process topology (driver interpreter → chain environment → reservation interpreter → custody worker) over the exact clone, ledger, arguments and full observation set, stopping before append; its non-authorizing receipt binds plan, ledger head, code digests and effective interpreter identity, and a changed interpreter or input invalidates it; the probe is booted out and its processes proven gone. (4) Regressions: successful metadata probe followed by a stalled governed read through the real reservation CLI (a FIFO withholding EOF or a filesystem read barrier, never a mocked readiness), refusal within budget plus cleanup tolerance, unchanged ledger bytes, lease reacquirable, no late worker activity; several slow observations exhaust one shared budget; slow-within-budget success; hash mismatch stays calibration_ledger_custody_invalid; writer preflight and under-lease stalls refuse without starting a slot; missing or stale launchd probe receipt blocks the arm. (5) Runbook: treat every Homebrew Python replacement as invalidating the launchd access probe and rerun it. No change to any measurement, instrument, gate, or claim constant.

acceptance.summary: Before any per-phase energy number (prefill, decode, KV, speculative decode, MoE routing) reaches a paper draft, an executed check proves the phase intervals form a true partition of the request span: pairwise disjoint, covering (the phase durations sum to the span within the timestamp resolution), and sequenced by monotonic timestamps; a decomposition that overlaps or leaves a gap is refused with the offending intervals named, and the check's output is cited by the Paper C phase table. PHASE-PARTITION-INVARIANT-01.goal: Stop double-counting before it starts. Paper C's contribution is per-phase energy (prefill vs decode, KV, speculative decode, MoE), which is a sum over phase intervals of the request span; the SIGARCH post shows a published cost model whose four intervals overlapped, so the sum exceeded the whole. An executed partition invariant (disjoint, covering, sequenced) applied before any phase number is drafted makes that class of error impossible to publish; it is cheap (timestamps already exist in the capture records) and zero-presence for Ed.

PROBE-DRIVER-COPY-BINDING-01.goal: PROBE_CODE_PATHS in joulewise/night_agent_install.py:641-648 is the list of program files whose contents are hashed and recorded in the arm-time probe receipt as code_digests, so that editing any of them after a successful probe makes the install refuse. Every path in that list is resolved against plan.measurement_root, the measurement clone of the repository, so the receipt binds the measurement clone's copy of scripts/run_night.py. The night LaunchAgent (the macOS launchd job that actually runs the night) executes a different copy: the plist's @@REPO@@ placeholder is substituted with the DRIVER checkout, whose only binding is plan.repo_head, the git commit id of that checkout's committed head. A committed change to the driver checkout is therefore caught, but an uncommitted working-tree edit to the driver checkout's scripts/run_night.py after a successful probe changes what launchd will execute and leaves the receipt valid. The same gap covers any other driver-checkout program the plist executes.

WATCHDOG-BOOTID-CLOCK-STEP-01.goal: The watchdog in scripts/magistrate_watchdog.py uses a boot id (its reboot detector, a string built from sysctl kern.boottime) to associate a saved backoff wait with a machine boot. When a saved backoff deadline exists, reset_backoff_after_reboot compares the stored string with the current one and, on any difference, emits backoff_reset_after_reboot and clears the backoff deadlines. On 2026-09-16 at 22:57:31 PDT (events.jsonl epoch 1789624651.734894, immediately before transition sequence 174 FENCED → CLOCK_UNCERTAIN), the stored value was kern.boottime:{ sec = 1789527324, usec = 351165 } and the observed value kern.boottime:{ sec = 1789527324, usec = 277634 }, both followed by the same human-readable date: the same boot second, with a 73,531 µs difference in the microsecond field. The machine had not rebooted: kern.boottime sec was unchanged, and the interactive session and the previous activation's 20:59 stand-down were on this boot. As recorded in launch record 00, macOS adjusts kern.boottime when the wall clock is stepped; the machine had just been moved and its clock re-synchronised, also triggering CLOCK_UNCERTAIN at that instant. The exact-string comparison therefore mistook a clock step for a reboot. The spurious backoff reset was benign here, but boot-keyed logic sharing this string can misclassify a clock step as a reboot or vice versa: current_boot_id (:500-519), apply_backoff (:1371), reset_backoff_after_reboot (:1398-1412), and the clean-exit cooldown (:1719-1721) in scripts/magistrate_watchdog.py.
